title: Induction principle for separated quasi-compact opens
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let P be a property of quasi-compact open subschemes of X. Assume P holds for every affine open, and assume that whenever U is quasi-compact open and V is affine open, P holds for U, V, and U intersect V, then P holds for U union V. Then P holds for every separated quasi-compact open subscheme W of X.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 08DR (coherent-lemma-induction-principle), proof, first induction for separated quasi-compact opens

proof.text: Inside the separated open W, intersections of affine opens A,B contained in W are affine: pull back along W.ι, use IsAffineOpen.inf in W.toScheme, then map the intersection back along the open immersion. This is the absolute case of the affine-intersection statement.

Use Mathlib compact_open_induction_on, whose proof is induction on a finite affine cover, for the strengthened property Q(U): if U is contained in W, then P(U) and P(U intersect T) for every affine T contained in W. The empty case is the affine hypothesis. At a step U union V contained in W, the inductive hypothesis gives P(U), P(U intersect V), and P(U intersect T). The gluing hypothesis gives P(U union V). For each affine T contained in W, V intersect T is affine by the preceding step; U intersect T is quasi-compact by IsCompact.inter_of_isOpen using quasi-separatedness of X. The inductive hypothesis with the affine V intersect T gives P(U intersect V intersect T). Apply the gluing hypothesis to U intersect T and V intersect T, and distribute intersection over union. Finally Q(W) implies P(W).
